parsed.why: Strong state protections (anti-discrimination, hate-crime, panic-defence abolition, working enforcement) offset national exposure; but care bans for minors, sports restrictions and birth-certificate surgery requirement keep it below full acceptance tier.

Lowest-risk division: broad protections, sanctuary city, no facility bans, sports bills vetoed or stalled; mild gaps (no hate-crime statute, dormant sodomy residue) and no statewide hate-crime recourse hold it under 0.60.

Top Do-Not-Travel tier: enforced birth-certificate restroom law with ID checks, hostile school-district prosecutions, no LGR, 44 trans killings (2008–25), parental-rights statute, care and expression bans; high-risk band.

Criminalised restroom use reaching private businesses (hospital, restaurant, gas station) with up to a year jail — universal-exposure tier-1; no enforcement record, X licences, pending suit, but harsher than any other ban.

Worst tier: first state to strip gender-identity protections outright, preemption blocking local remedies, school facilities rule binding visitors statewide; no enforcement evidence, no specific facility ban outside schools, but law and enforcement posture deeply hostile.
